title: Understanding Maintenance and Family Rights
summary: What maintenance means, who can claim it, and how protection laws help families in difficulty.
sectionRefs: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 144, formerly CrPC 125)
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

body.text: Family disputes are painful, and the law tries to protect the weaker member, especially children and dependent spouses or parents. Understanding the basics helps you act calmly.

items: A person who cannot maintain themselves can seek a monthly allowance from a spouse or, in some cases, from children or parents.
It applies across religions under the BNSS provision on maintenance.
The court looks at the needs of the claimant and the means of the person paying.

body.text: The provision on maintenance (Section 144 of the BNSS, earlier Section 125 CrPC) is a quick remedy meant to stop destitution, and it covers wives, children and parents.

items: Physical, emotional, sexual and economic abuse are all covered by the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
A woman can seek a protection order, a residence order and monetary relief.
Help is available through Protection Officers and the women's helpline 181.

body.text: If you or someone at home is in immediate danger, call 112 first. Safety comes before any legal step.
Keep a diary of incidents, medical records and any messages. Documentation helps a court act faster.

practicalSteps: For immediate danger, call 112; for counselling and shelter, call 181.
Contact the District Legal Services Authority for free legal aid.
File a maintenance application before the Magistrate where you live.
Keep records of income, expenses and any threats or abuse.
exceptions: Maintenance can be refused if the claimant is able to maintain themselves or has remarried, among other grounds.
Personal laws of different communities have their own separate provisions as well.

faqs.a: The BNSS provision applies to any person who cannot maintain themselves, though it is most often used by women, children and parents.

faqs.q: Does a wife need to prove cruelty to get maintenance?
faqs.a: No. Maintenance focuses on the inability to maintain oneself, not on proving cruelty. Cruelty is relevant to other reliefs such as divorce.

sources.label: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - India Code

misconceptions.fact: It can be claimed by children and parents too, and by any person unable to maintain themselves.
